explanation_unavailable: No detailed explanation is available for this rule or configuration.
explanation_hamilton_description: This method computes each option’s exact quota: the fractional number of seats it is entitled to. It rounds this down to the lower quota and gives each option that many seats. Remaining seats go to the options with the largest remainders: the quota minus the lower quota.
explanation_hamilton_ties: There were ties. The possible Hamilton apportionments follow the table above except for these options: {options}. Of these, exactly {extra, plural, one {# option receives one seat above its lower quota} other {# options receive one seat above their lower quotas}}; the remaining {remaining, plural, one {# option receives its lower quota} other {# options receive their lower quotas}}.
explanation_quota_properties: This variation of the D’Hondt/Jefferson method is house monotone and satisfies both lower and upper quota.
explanation_quota_description: Repeatedly select the largest quotient in the table (votes divided by 1, 2, 3, and so on) and give its option one seat. An option cannot receive more seats than its upper quota. If it has reached this limit, move to the next-largest quotient belonging to an option that has not reached its upper quota.
explanation_fewer_seats: There are {seats, plural, one {# available seat} other {# available seats}} and {options, plural, one {# option} other {# options}}. When there are fewer seats than options, this divisor method gives one seat to each of the {seats, plural, one {# highest-voted option} other {# highest-voted options}} and no seats to the others.
explanation_divide_votes: For each option, divide its vote total by {divisor}. The result is its quotient.
explanation_round_down: Round the quotient down to an integer (take the floor) to obtain the number of seats.
explanation_round_nearest: Round the quotient to the nearest integer to obtain the number of seats for the option.
explanation_round_geometric: Use geometric rounding: if the quotient lies between the integers n and n + 1, calculate their geometric mean x = √(n(n + 1)). Round up when the quotient is greater than x, and down when it is less than x.
explanation_round_harmonic: Use harmonic rounding: if the quotient lies between the integers n and n + 1, calculate their harmonic mean x = n(n + 1) / (n + 0.5). Round up when the quotient is greater than x, and down when it is less than x.
explanation_round_up: Round the quotient up to an integer (take the ceiling) to obtain the number of seats.
explanation_table_description: Create a table with one row per option. Each cell contains the option’s votes divided by the column’s divisor. Highlight the {seats, plural, one {# largest value} other {# largest values}} in green. Each green cell gives its option one seat.
explanation_divisor_ties: There were ties. The possible apportionments follow the table above except that seats can be reassigned among these tied options: {options}. Currently, these options received an extra seat: {receiving}.
explanation_pb_comparison: The committee chosen by the greedy algorithm is preferred by {greedy, plural, one {# voter} other {# voters}}, while the committee chosen by the method of equal shares is preferred by {mes, plural, one {# voter} other {# voters}}.
